chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Umar ibn Yazeed, that he heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

'Indeed, in the night there is a time which a Muslim servant matches by praying and supplicating to Allah during it, except that he is answered during every night.' I said, 'May Allah keep you well! So which time from the night is it?' He said: 'When half the night passes, during the first sixth of the remaining half.'

key_terms.اسْتُجِيبَ لَهُ: he is answered (his supplication is accepted)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific time in the night when supplications are guaranteed to be answered according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual potency of the 'last third' of the night, a time traditionally associated with divine proximity and the acceptance of du'a. The specific calculation—identifying the first sixth of the remaining half—reflects the precise temporal understanding found in Shia jurisprudence for organizing night prayers (Salat al-Layl). It underscores the principle that consistent devotion during this auspicious window guarantees a response, reinforcing the link between disciplined worship and divine mercy.

en.hubeali:
From him, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, 
(It has been narrated) from Umar Bin Yazeed having heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:

‘During the night there is a time what is compatible for a submissive servant to pray Salāt and supplicate to Allahazwj during it, except that it would be Answered to him during every night’. I said, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! So which time from the night is it?’ Heasws said: ‘When half the night passes by, during the first sixth of the remaining half’.
en.sarwar: 19. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from ‘Umar ibn Yazid say the following: “I heard abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘

In the night there is an hour in which if a Muslim performs Salah (prayer) and appeals before Allah for a wish; his prayer is answered every night. I (the narrator) then asked saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, which hour is it?’ The Imam replied, ‘It is in the first one-sixth of the second half of the night.”’
